FX-RIM-001.says: The settings as they start: white light from 45 degrees, the upper right, width 3, softness 1, intensity 100, normal. The block's top two rows and right two columns turn white, with a fainter third; the red dot, alone, turns wholly white, and itself shades the line's end at (12, 7), whose point toward the light falls beside the dot; the empty pixels stay empty and the block's lower left stays skin.

FX-RIM-002.says: Direction 0, light from straight above: the block's top three rows turn white and the fourth takes a trace of it; the soft edge, whose own covering is half, is half lit down its whole length.

FX-RIM-003.says: Direction 90, light from the right: the block's right three columns turn white, all but (11, 5), whose point three pixels to the right is the red dot, which shades it; the soft edge on the left is not lit.

FX-RIM-004.says: Direction 180, light from below: the line along the block's foot turns white, with the two rows of skin above it, and the third row a trace.

FX-RIM-005.says: Direction 270, light from the left: the soft edge turns wholly white at its half covering, and the block's left two columns beside it; the third, whose point three pixels to the left is the soft edge's centre, is half lit.

FX-RIM-006.says: Width 0, softness 0: rim = 1 - covering, so only the soft edge, half covered, is lit, by 127/255; every fully covered pixel is untouched.

FX-RIM-007.says: Width 1: a rim about a pixel deep on the top and right.

FX-RIM-008.says: Width 2.5: between widths 1 and 3, the point sampled falling between pixels.

FX-RIM-009.says: Softness 0, direction 0: the rim is hard, the top three rows wholly white and the rest untouched, where FX-RIM-002, at softness 1, gave the fourth row a trace.

FX-RIM-011.says: Intensity 50: every pixel halfway between the drawing and FX-RIM-001.

FX-RIM-012.says: Colour #ffb040, an orange, blend normal: FX-RIM-001's rim in orange.

FX-RIM-013.says: Colour #ffb040, blend add: the orange added onto the skin, brighter than white on its red, past what a screen reaches.

FX-RIM-014.says: Colour #ffb040, blend screen: lighter than the skin, never past white.

FX-RIM-015.says: Colour #ffb040, blend multiply: the rim darkens the skin toward orange, and red, fully lit, keeps its own red channel.

FX-RIM-016.says: FX-RIM-013 with the colour written in capitals, #FFB040: the same.

FX-RIM-017.says: Direction keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 180 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is FX-RIM-002, frame 2, at 90, FX-RIM-003, and frame 4 FX-RIM-004.

FX-RIM-018.says: Width keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 4 at frame 4, linear: the rim deepens, width 2 at frame 2.

FX-RIM-019.says: Intensity eased from 0 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4 on a curve that overshoots: at frame 2 it would pass 100, is held at 100, and is FX-RIM-001; frame 0 is the drawing.

FX-RIM-020.says: Direction 450, a turn and a quarter: FX-RIM-003 exactly.

FX-RIM-021.says: FX-RIM-001 moved three pixels right: the same, moved; the layer does not grow.

FX-RIM-022.says: Width 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RIM-023.says: Intensity -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RIM-024.says: Softness 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RIM-025.says: Direction -3601, below -3600. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RIM-026.says: Width keyed to 150 at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RIM-027.says: Blend "overlay", which is not a blend. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-RIM-028.says: Colour "#fff", written in three digits, not six. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
